title: Sequential colimits represent homotopy colimits
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and let $\mathcal A=\Ab(\mathcal C)$, or let $\mathcal O$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal A=\Mod(\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $E_0^\bullet\xrightarrow{f_0}E_1^\bullet\xrightarrow{f_1}\cdots$ be a sequence of cochain complexes in $\mathcal A$, and write $Q:\mathrm{CoCh}(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal A)$ for localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Put $A^\bullet=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}E_n^\bullet$ (degreewise coproduct), and define $u:A^\bullet\to A^\bullet$ by $u\iota_n=\iota_n-\iota_{n+1}f_n$. Let $L^\bullet=\varinjlim_n E_n^\bullet$ be the degreewise colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], with $q:A^\bullet\to L^\bullet$ induced by its structure maps. Then the canonical chain map $p:\operatorname{Cone}(u)\to L^\bullet$, equal to $q$ on $A^\bullet$ and zero on the shifted summand $A^\bullet[1]$, is a quasi-isomorphism. Moreover $Q(A^\bullet)$ with maps $Q(\iota_n)$ is the coproduct of $Q(E_n^\bullet)$ in $D(\mathcal A)$, and its cone triangle exhibits $Q(\operatorname{Cone}(u))$ as a homotopy colimit of that sequence [def-kun-truncations]. The isomorphism $Q(p)$ identifies this homotopy colimit with $Q(L^\bullet)$; transporting the cone triangle along $Q(p)$ exhibits $Q(L^\bullet)$ itself as a homotopy colimit. This includes the small etale site with any constant commutative coefficient ring, in particular $\mathbf Z/n$. No boundedness or monicity of the $f_n$ is required.

proof.text: For abelian sheaves use exact filtered colimits. For module sheaves use the exact forgetful functor to abelian sheaves: Mathlib HasExactColimitsOfShape.domain_of_functor reflects finite limits and preserves filtered colimits. Shrink the filtered-index universe to Type 0. The same exactness holds in cochain complexes degreewise by HomologicalComplex.hasExactColimitsOfShape. CountableAB4.of_countableAB5 gives exact countable coproducts in each coefficient category.
Apply [lem-kun-sequential-telescope-mono] in the abelian category of cochain complexes to the specified coproduct B and telescope map u. This gives monicity without a monic-transition hypothesis.

The coproduct equations and the cocone equations imply uq=0, checked after every coprojection. A morphism r from B with ur=0 gives a cocone on E, since the equality on each consecutive transition is precisely (iota_n - f_n iota_{n+1})r=0. The universal property of L therefore gives a unique factorization through q. Thus q is a cokernel of u. Together with monicity this is the asserted short exact sequence of complexes. The Lean helper telescope_cokernel constructs this cokernel universal property explicitly.

Use mappingCone.descShortComplex for the short exact sequence. Its restrictions are q and zero, and [lem-pc-cone-short-exact-quasi-iso] gives its quasi-isomorphism. Localization makes its image invertible; asIso provides the required e with e.hom=Q.map p.

Apply [lem-kun-derived-countable-sums-exact] and transport preservation from its chosen degreewise coproduct to the specified B. This yields the actual coprojections Q.map (B.inj n). Essential surjectivity of Q then gives all countable coproducts in the derived category: choose complex preimages for an arbitrary countable family and transport its mapped coproduct across the component isomorphisms.

The localized mapping-cone triangle is distinguished. Triangle.isoMk transports its third vertex along e; its second square is Q(inr)Q(p)=Q(q), and its third square cancels e.hom with e.inv. For either triangle identify its first two vertices with the chosen derived coproduct using the unique coproduct isomorphism. Checking each coprojection, additivity of Q and hu identify its first arrow with identity minus successor. The remaining arrows transport with this coproduct isomorphism and its shifted inverse. This supplies both instances of [def-kun-truncations], with the same countable-coproduct structure.
